samasa.sense: Brahmāṇī and the other Mothers of chapter 8

morph.note: Perfect of √गम्, third plural: reduplicated ज-ग्म्-उः with loss of the root vowel. लयं जग्मुः, ‘went to dissolution’, is the idiom for being absorbed.
Imperfect of √अस्, with augment and the inserted ī of the adādi class before a single-consonant ending: आस्-ई-त्.

mantras.anvaya: ततः ब्रह्माणीप्रमुखाः ताः समस्ताः देव्यः तस्याः देव्याः तनौ लयं जग्मुः। तदा अम्बिका एका एव आसीत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: the goddesses (subject, with three qualifiers) ‘go to dissolution’ in her body; then Ambikā is alone.
mantras.lit: Then all those goddesses, headed by Brahmāṇī, went to absorption in the body of that Goddess. Then Ambikā was alone, one only.
mantras.tr: Then all those goddesses, Brahmāṇī and the rest, dissolved into the Goddess’s body, and Ambikā stood alone.

comm.t: The narrator confirms in action what the Goddess has just said (10.5): the Mothers enter her body and vanish. The verse repeats her own word, एका एव, of the Goddess as she now stands.
लय is also the word for the world’s dissolution (pralaya). Read in that light in the Śākta tradition, the powers are not dismissed but resolved into their source.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) calls the Goddess लयकरी (739), ‘she who brings about dissolution’. The name is general; here the dissolution is of her own manifested forms.

morph.note: Two constructions are possible. (1) Relative pronoun, object of आस्थिता: ‘that (state) which I had assumed here in many forms … that is withdrawn’, with तत् as its correlative — taken here. (2) Adverbial यत् = यदा, ‘when I stood here in many forms … that was withdrawn’; then तत् refers to the plurality itself. The sense is the same.
आ + √स्था ‘to take one’s stand on, assume’ is transitive; its past participle can be active in sense and take an object (यत्): ‘(I) who had assumed’.
सम् + √हृ ‘to draw together, withdraw’ — the same verb that names the dissolution of the world (saṃhāra). मया is its agent.
√स्था forms its present stem by reduplication (ष्ठा → तिष्ठ-), listed with the bhvādi class.

mantras.anvaya: अहं विभूत्या इह बहुभिः रूपैः यत् आस्थिता, तत् मया संहृतम्। (अधुना) एका एव आजौ तिष्ठामि। स्थिरः भव।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative-correlative sentence (यत् … आस्थिता, तत् … संहृतम्), a statement (एका एव तिष्ठामि) and an imperative (स्थिरः भव).
mantras.lit: What I had assumed here, through my power of manifestation, in many forms — that has been withdrawn by me. I stand alone in battle. Be steady!
mantras.tr: Through my power I stood here in many forms; those I have withdrawn. Now I stand alone on the battlefield — stand firm!
mantras.tr_note: The tr follows the reading यत् = ‘what (state)’, simplified to ‘those (forms) I have withdrawn’; ‘now’ is supplied.

comm.t: The Goddess explains what Śumbha has seen: the many forms were her own power (विभूति) displayed; she has withdrawn them, and now meets him alone. स्थिरो भव is a challenge: ‘hold your ground’.

The verb संहृतम् belongs to the vocabulary of cosmic dissolution (saṃhāra), and in the Śākta tradition the verse is read in that light: what the Goddess projects she can take back, and the manifold is her own, not another’s. The word विभूति is the one the Bhagavad Gītā uses for the divine manifestations in its tenth chapter.
A modern reading: the Goddess answers the charge of dependence not by argument but by demonstration — she withdraws every helper and stays.

morph.note: Perfect middle of प्र + √वृत्: reduplicated व-वृत्-, ending -ए. प्र + √वृत् ‘to set forth, begin’ is the stock verb for a battle beginning.
Genitive absolute (षष्ठी used ‘in disregard’): ‘with all the gods and asuras looking on’. The participle agrees with the genitive nouns, not with the subject of the main verb.

mantras.anvaya: ततः देव्याः शुम्भस्य च उभयोः दारुणं युद्धं सर्वदेवानाम् असुराणां च पश्यतां प्रववृते।
mantras.anvaya_en: Main clause ततः … युद्धं प्रववृते, with the genitives देव्याः शुम्भस्य च उभयोः naming the combatants and a genitive absolute (सर्वदेवानाम् असुराणां च पश्यताम्).
mantras.lit: Then the terrible battle of both — of the Goddess and of Śumbha — began, while all the gods and the asuras were looking on.
mantras.tr: Then, as all the gods and the asuras looked on, a terrible battle began between the two, the Goddess and Śumbha.

comm.t: The final duel begins. Both armies are now spectators: the gods and the surviving asuras watch the two combatants alone.
A modern reading: the genitive absolute (पश्यताम्) makes both worlds witnesses. The last battle is fought in the open, before gods and asuras alike, so that its outcome cannot be disputed.
